cover_options.text: Mistral launched a 1-trillion-parameter AI model it pitches for cyber defense
Mistral says its new model is the best open one from the US or Europe. No weights yet.
Mistral's new model scores 38 on an independent index. The leader scores 58.

headline.text: A preview now, weights at the end of October

body.text: On Oct 6, Mistral released Mistral Large 4, nicknamed Le Chonk, as a public preview through its API. Mistral says it has 1 trillion parameters, 49 billion active. The weights are not out yet.

headline.text: Mistral pitches it as a cyber defense tool

body.text: Mistral says closed models' safety filters block legitimate defensive work, attackers jailbreak them anyway, and losing provider access mid-incident is itself a security risk. ML4 can run on-premise.

headline.text: US closed models had already hit limits this year

body.text: In June, the Trump administration temporarily restricted OpenAI and Anthropic model distribution over cyberattack concerns. Hugging Face used Z.ai's GLM 5.2 after US closed models' guardrails blocked its breach defense.

headline.text: Mistral also sells it as a European answer

body.text: Trained from scratch on its own European compute with Nvidia Grace Blackwell GPUs, Mistral says. It will also offer a European variant run fully under European law.

headline.text: 82% on a cyber test. Mistral says rivals refuse it.

body.text: Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra score near zero on this test because they refuse it, Mistral says. Artificial Analysis lists ML4's 82% but compares it only with MiMo-V2.6-Pro (79%) and GPT-6 Luna (78%).

headline.text: 38 on an independent index. The leader scores 58.

body.text: On the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, ML4 is up from 9 for Mistral Large 3 but well below Claude Opus 5.5 (Max) at 58. The-decoder.com says it trails leading closed models and several Chinese open-weight ones.

headline.text: Best open model? Two related but different claims

body.text: Per Mistral, ML4 is the best open-weight model from the US or Europe. Artificial Analysis calls it the most intelligent model from outside the US and China. It lists ML4 as proprietary until weights ship.

headline.text: What Mistral hasn't said yet

body.text: Security firms, vetted partners and government agencies are red-teaming a reduced-moderation ML4, Mistral says. Mistral does not explain how ML4 tells research from attack prep. License terms are unknown.

caption.text:
French AI lab Mistral launched a public preview of Mistral Large 4, nicknamed Le Chonk, on October 6. Mistral pitches the model, which it says has 1 trillion parameters, for cyber defense.

Mistral says it is the best open-weight model from the US or Europe. Open-weight means the trained parameters are released so others can modify and self-host the model, and Mistral's weights are due at the end of October, so the label is still pending. On the independent Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, Mistral Large 4 scores 38. Claude Opus 5.5 (Max) leads at 58. Mistral also says closed models' safety filters block legitimate defensive work. It has not explained how its model tells legitimate vulnerability research from attack prep, and the license terms are not out yet.

Would you rather run your cyber defense on a model you host yourself or one a provider controls?

Follow Helios Group to see what the Mistral Large 4 weights and license look like when they ship.

Source: the-decoder.com, October 6, 2026. Additional reporting: Wired, TechCrunch, CNBC, Artificial Analysis (LinkedIn), Mistral on X.

edit_notes: Cover 1 chosen: Mistral is well_known, so it leads; the cyber-defense pitch is the news, and the benchmark gap is saved for the slides.
No quote slides: every quote is single-source, and the pitch and sovereignty points are told through attributed F8 and F9 instead.
Nickname Le Chonk written without quotation marks because it is not a QUOTES entry.
GPU count (3,800 vs 4,000) and context window (1M vs 512k) left out because sources disagree and the brief leaves both unresolved.
Mistral's 82% claim about Claude and GPT refusing is attributed to Mistral on the slide, and the slide notes Artificial Analysis only compares with MiMo and GPT-6 Luna.
Slide 8 shows the Mistral claim and the Artificial Analysis claim side by side, since the brief calls them related but different.
Background slide uses B2 only (June restrictions and the Hugging Face case), kept to the facts and left out the unattributed Wired claim about US models attacking companies.
Launch discount and the preview price left out because the brief doesn't settle whether $0.68/$2.09 is the discounted price.
Series D (B1) and Renda quote (July, not about launch) left out as off-story.
Pierre Stock's N6 comparison with Chinese competitors left out; it is single-source and not needed.
Caption glosses open-weight from the TERMS list (CNBC) and keeps every Mistral hedge.
